subject: Provisional stability guardrail exception request for Polaris-2.1f variant
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-11T09:14:00Z
Subject: Provisional stability guardrail exception request for Polaris-2.1f variant

Team —

Quick summary: OrbitalAI (prospect) wants to pilot Polaris-2.1f for a Q3 product demo. The model shows ~18% lower latency and 12% cost/per-token advantage after our new kernel path, but Neha's safety compatibility suite flagged an elevated rate of rare hallucination patterns in one targeted scenario (user-provided long-context prompts). Given the commercial opportunity and the measurable infra benefits, I’m requesting a provisional guardrail exception: temporarily pin the serving variant to 2.1f for OrbitalAI’s dedicated route while we ship a micro-patch and run extended canaries.

What I need from each function (high level):
- Product (Laura): approve the provisional customer-scoped pin and confirm OK with the demo timeline (2 weeks).
- Applied ML (Neha): confirm test failure modes, proposed mitigations, and acceptance criteria for the roll-forward patch.
- Infra/Serving (Dev): confirm feasibility to serve a variant-specific routing rule + short-lived pin and what runtime telemetry we need.
- QA (Hannah): sign off on canary test plan and gate for rollback.
- Sales/Leadership (Marissa): if you can OK a 10% one-time credit for the pilot if we need to pause.

Attachments: polaris_2.1f_safety_compat_report.pdf (summary + failing examples), provisional_rollout plan (spreadsheet).

Constraints / notes:
- This must be scoped to OrbitalAI’s route only (no global pin).
- Maximum provisional duration requested: 14 calendar days from approval.
- We must prevent automatic global rollouts, and ensure the fallback to 2.0.9 is immediate on critical regression.

I recommend we use the provisional pattern (ROUT-412) — infra already has the extension but needs the formal exception and documented acceptance criteria. Happy to jump on a 15-min sync after initial replies.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Provisional stability guardrail exception request for Polaris-2.1f variant

Vivek — thanks for the clear ask. A few follow-ups before I greenlight:

1) Demo window: when exactly is the OrbitalAI demo? We should align the provisional period to end at least 72 hours before the demo for safety.
2) Success criteria: I need a concise acceptance checklist (safety false-positive/negative thresholds, latency targets, error rates) that Product can sign off on.
3) Commercials: Marissa, please advise on the proposed pilot credit and whether Sales is comfortable making that commit conditional on a rollback trigger.

Neha, can you paste a short list of the top 3 failing prompt classes inline (no attachments needed) — that'll help me prioritize the acceptance checklist.

If we’re all aligned, I can approve a scoped provisional pin for OrbitalAI for up to 14 days, contingent on the acceptance criteria and an infra rollback playbook.

- Laura
Laura Bennett

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Provisional stability guardrail exception request for Polaris-2.1f variant

Quick findings from the safety/compat run (high level):

Failing prompt classes (top 3):
1) Interleaved long instruction + code blocks > 12k tokens — hallucination rate spike (confabbed function names)
2) Persona-switch prompts that chain role-play requests across turns — loss of persona anchoring
3) Sparse-fact retrieval style prompts with many short citations — hallucinated citations with high confidence

Root cause hypothesis: the new kernel path improves throughput but changes attention accumulation precision slightly for very long contexts — leads to degraded KV cache conditioning in edge cases. We see no privacy or data-leak issues.

Mitigations / acceptance criteria proposal:
- Immediate: block Polaris-2.1f for any route with user-supplied context > 10k tokens until patch. (This can be enforced at routing-time.)
- Short-term patch (48–72h): tighten attention normalization in kernel and run quantized regression tests. Passing criteria: hallucination frequency reduced to within 1.5x baseline on the failing suites.
- Canary targets: 5k requests over 48h split by prompt class, with no critical regression (defined as >=3 critical hallucinations in the same prompt class).

I’ve attached the full compat report (polaris_2.1f_safety_compat_report.pdf). I can author the acceptance checklist for Product to sign off.

- Neha
Neha Kapoor
Applied ML, Model Safety
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T13:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Provisional stability guardrail exception request for Polaris-2.1f variant

Thanks — technical feasibility notes:

- We can implement a customer-scoped variant pin via the routing table for OrbitalAI’s dedicated route. It’s a config flag (route.variant_override) and we already have a provisional TTL param.
- Blocking by context-length is doable at ingress (router) with a straightforward header check; I'll add that rule as part of the rollout spreadsheet.
- Telemetry: we need to emit the following extra metrics during the canary window: per-route hallucination markers (neha’s signal), runtime quantization drift, attention-checksum deltas, and request path (to ensure no accidental global routing).
- Fallback: immediate fallback to 2.0.9 is implemented as an atomic routing change and tested in staging. The only manual step: an owner must confirm the rollback in PagerDuty. I suggest we add a single-step rollback runbook to ROUT-412.

I’ve attached runtime_fallback_patch.diff.txt and a provisional_rollout sheet with the TTL values. If Product signs the acceptance checklist I can schedule a midnight canary (US-PST) to minimize customer impact.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Provisional stability guardrail exception request for Polaris-2.1f variant

QA plan summary:

1) Canary matrix: run the three failing classes at scale — 5k requests / class, seeded from the failing corpus.
2) Monitoring: automated watchdog to surface hallucination patterns and surge in user-facing errors; thresholds set to Neha’s ‘critical regression’ definition.
3) Rollback criteria: any critical regression observed in two consecutive 1-hour windows or >0.5% error increase in user-facing latency triggers immediate rollback.
4) Post-mortem: 72-hour investigation window after canary; if issues persist, we hold the pin and revert to 2.0.9 globally for OrbitalAI.

I will own the canary execution and will update the provisional_rollout spreadsheet with timestamps and the exact test harness commands.

— Hannah
